text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and grounded in the card. 18.2% of 988 claims vs 4.4% expected, the risk-adjusted score of 8.35, z of 2.07, and 21% low-complexity share all match. Documentation figures also match: 34 documented claims, 11 of 14 99215 claims below billed (79%), and 2 of 16 notes with no lab line. The cited claims fit their sentences: C0085805, C0085943 and C0086118 are below-billed examples, and the three low-complexity claims are correct. The language is cautious (\"reason to review the records, not a finding\"), and next steps are concrete (request charts, coder re-score, audit trail). Weaknesses: the unmatched \"6\" is most likely the count of cited claims or a similar artifact, not a real error. The \"5% comparison\" figure and the note-check shares (problems 18%, late 3%, unsigned 0%, data 6%) are not on the card and may come from tool output. The audit-trail step is vague about why it is needed, because the summary states none was received. The summary does not weigh the 3 supported 99215 claims against the pattern. The mix of documentation examples and low-complexity claims in one list is slightly confusing, and C0085805 is a 94-year-old with 4 conditions documented as moderate, which complicates the narrative. The \"problems 18%\" note check is loosely interpreted as addressing fewer problems than the level implies.","problems":["Note-check shares (problems 18%, late 3%, unsigned 0%, data 6%) and the 5% comparison rate are not clearly traceable to the card","Low-complexity example claims have no documentation reviewed, so they support only the complexity point, not the below-billed point","The audit-trail request is generic, given that no audit trail was received","Does not mention that 3 documented 99215 claims supported the billed level","The next step on random sampling is boilerplate and not specific to this case"]}
